name: AIMS Analyzer Diagnosis Rules
description: Open rule pack for GC/FTIR process analyzer fault diagnosis

rules.diagnosis: Component reading shows upward drift relative to recent baseline. Likely causes: calibration gas depleted, sample line contamination, or detector aging.
rules.recommendation: 1) Verify calibration gas cylinder pressure and expiry. 2) Run multi-point calibration. 3) Check sample filter and probe for deposits.

rules.diagnosis: Component reading shows downward drift. Possible sample dilution, carrier gas leak, or detector sensitivity loss.
rules.recommendation: 1) Leak-check sample and carrier lines. 2) Confirm purge/carrier flow setpoints. 3) Inspect detector (FID flame / TCD filament).

rules.diagnosis: Elevated noise or spiking on the channel. Common causes: electrical interference, unstable utility gases, dirty column or detector.
rules.recommendation: 1) Check grounding and shield on signal cables. 2) Stabilize H2/Air/He supply pressures. 3) Condition or replace column if residual noise persists.

rules.diagnosis: Slow dynamic response to process changes. Often caused by long sample lag, restricted probe, or excessive filter volume.
rules.recommendation: 1) Measure sample transport time. 2) Clean/replace sample filter. 3) Shorten sample line if lag exceeds design.

rules.diagnosis: Methane concentration elevated vs operating envelope. Could be true process upset or analyzer bias after calibration shift.
rules.recommendation: 1) Cross-check with lab sample. 2) Review last calibration coefficients. 3) Inspect for sample line leak drawing in fuel gas.

rules.diagnosis: FID flame-out signature. Hydrogen or air supply interruption is the most frequent root cause.
rules.recommendation: 1) Confirm H2 and air pressures at analyzer. 2) Relight FID per SOP. 3) Check igniter and jet for blockage.

rules.diagnosis: Component sum outside 99-104% band indicates calibration or missing component issue.
rules.recommendation: 1) Recalibrate major components. 2) Verify all reported peaks are integrated. 3) Check for unreported heavies (Hexane+).

rules.diagnosis: CO2 concentration elevated. Could be a true process upset, or a TCD/NDIR sensor bias after a calibration shift.
rules.recommendation: 1) Cross-check with lab sample or a secondary analyzer. 2) Verify CO2 span gas certificate and last calibration date. 3) Check sample system for air in-leakage.

rules.diagnosis: H2S reading elevated — safety-relevant. Could reflect a genuine sour-gas upset or sensor drift/contamination.
rules.recommendation: 1) Treat as a potential safety event until confirmed otherwise; follow site H2S procedure. 2) Verify with a portable/lab reference. 3) Inspect sensor for poisoning/contamination and recalibrate.

rules.diagnosis: Nitrogen reading has moved outside its typical operating band. On a GC this is often the first symptom of a carrier-gas or column issue rather than a real process change.
rules.recommendation: 1) Check carrier gas (He/N2) supply pressure and purity. 2) Verify column condition and oven temperature. 3) Confirm all other components still sum correctly.

rules.diagnosis: Heavy-ends (C5+/C6+) reading elevated. Common causes: liquid carryover/slugging into the sample system, or column bleed mis-integrated as a heavy peak.
rules.recommendation: 1) Check sample probe location and knockout pot/filter for liquid carryover. 2) Verify sample line is heat-traced above dew point. 3) Review chromatogram integration around the heavies window.

rules.diagnosis: Sample system pressure below normal operating range, which can starve the analyzer and bias every component reading low.
rules.recommendation: 1) Check regulator setpoint and upstream tap/valve position. 2) Leak-check the sample line. 3) Confirm pump/eductor (if used) is operating.

rules.diagnosis: Analyzer/oven temperature running above setpoint, which can shift retention times and detector baselines.
rules.recommendation: 1) Check heater/controller for a stuck-on output. 2) Verify enclosure ventilation/cooling fan operation. 3) Re-run calibration once temperature is stable.

rules.diagnosis: Calibration span check has shifted outside tolerance versus the reference value. The analyzer is likely reading biased across the whole range, not just at this one point.
rules.recommendation: 1) Confirm calibration gas cylinder pressure, certificate, and expiry. 2) Repeat the span check to rule out a one-off bad injection. 3) If repeatable, run a full multi-point calibration and inspect the detector.

default.diagnosis: Insufficient symptom match in the open rule pack. Provide more context or connect an LLM (AI_API_KEY) for generative diagnosis.
default.recommendation: Collect recent trends, last calibration report, and utility gas status before escalating to vendor support.
